**Tidepool Build Plan**

**1. Persistent left sidebar — week timeline.** A narrow (~72px) forest-green rail runs the full page height, holding five circular nodes labeled M–F. Each node anchors to a page section (hero = Monday, features = midweek, pricing = Friday); the active section's node fills coral. This carries over the reference's signature structure and literally embodies "plan the week."

**2. Hero.** Two-thirds-width column right of the rail. One long, single-sentence headline in a warm serif (e.g., Fraunces) on deep forest green (#1B3A2F): "Bring your whole team into one shared plan that fills itself out every Monday morning, shows who's doing what at a glance, and quietly absorbs the status meeting so nobody has to ask what's on deck this week." A hand-drawn coral arrow curls from the headline to the product screenshot below, echoing the annotation motif. Headline in cream (#F6F1E7); CTA button in coral (#FF6F5E).

**3. Screenshot.** Tidepool's actual weekly board — columns per day, avatar chips on tasks — framed slightly tilted on a cream card for warmth.

**4. Feature trio.** Three columns on cream background, each with a thin-line green icon: shared weekly view, async standup updates, load-balancing across teammates. Copy stays concrete and verb-first ("See the whole week," "Replace the Monday meeting").

**5. Pull quote.** A customer quote from a team lead set in a monospace face (JetBrains Mono), coral opening quote mark, centered on the green background — carrying over the reference's mono-quote quirk: "We killed our Monday standup in week two. Tidepool just shows the week."

**6. Pricing.** Two cards (Free / Team), green outlines, coral highlight on the recommended plan.

**7. Footer.** Green rail continues to the floor; minimal links, one final coral CTA.
final:
**Tidepool Build Plan (rev. 2)**

**1. Week rail (persistent left sidebar).** Widen to 88px on cream so it reads as page furniture, not a dark strip; green nodes M–F double as scroll-spy nav. New: a thin coral "tide line" fills the rail top-to-bottom as the visitor scrolls — the page itself passes through a week, making the Tidepool metaphor literal. On mobile, the rail collapses to a five-dot progress bar pinned to the top.

**2. Hero.** Deep forest green (#1B3A2F) field, cream Fraunces headline, keeping the long single-sentence structure but ending sharper: "...so nobody opens Monday wondering what they own." The hand-drawn coral arrow now *draws itself* on load (SVG stroke animation) pointing to the screenshot. Two CTAs: coral primary "Start your week," ghost secondary "See a live board."

**3. Screenshot.** Real weekly board on a slightly tilted cream card, with three coral hotspot dots revealing tooltips that name features in place (avatars, drag-to-reschedule, Friday digest) — proof instead of caption.

**4. "How a week flows" — replaces the generic feature trio.** Three stacked rows keyed to the rail's nodes: *Monday — plan together in ten minutes; Wednesday — adjust async, no meeting; Friday — see what shipped.* Each pairs a thin-line green icon with a cropped fragment of real UI, so every claim is shown, not asserted.

**5. Pull quote + proof strip.** Customer quote in JetBrains Mono on green, coral quote mark, now with full attribution (name, role, team size) and a small strip of customer team logos beneath: "We killed our Monday standup in week two. Tidepool just shows the week."

**6. Pricing.** Free / Team ($8/seat), green-outlined cards, coral fill on the recommended plan. One trust line: "Every plan includes unlimited guests."

**7. Arrival + footer.** The tide line completes and the Friday node lights coral at page bottom — a deliberate payoff. Minimal links, one final coral button: "Plan your first week."

**Key upgrades:** the rail now narrates progress; features became a day-by-day story; description was swapped for demonstrable proof throughout.
